subject: Request: multi-vector uptime credit for brief partial degradation on /v1/generate
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@heliohealth.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-04-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent partial degradation observed on /v1/generate - request for credit

Hi Tessa,

We observed a brief but noticeable increase in 5xxs and latency for our service calls to /v1/generate this morning between ~09:05 and 09:40 PT. Impact: about 12% increased error rate and a handful of timed-out streaming responses. This affected our production traffic (customer-facing).

Attached are a small sample of request IDs and timestamps for cross-correlation (helio_sample_request_ids.csv). Can you confirm whether this is captured on your side and what portion, if any, is attributable to Redwood versus upstream peering issues? HelioHealth is requesting an initial credit estimate while we investigate.

Thanks,
Maria Gonzalez
Director, Platform Reliability
HelioHealth

--
HelioHealth support: support@heliohealth.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@heliohealth.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-04-07T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent partial degradation observed on /v1/generate - request for credit

Hi Maria — thanks for the sample IDs and the heads-up. We see matching client-side retries for the timestamps you provided. I'm looping in Jonas from our infra team to do a quick correlation against our edge and origin telemetry.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you confirm which POPs your traffic primarily hit during that window?
- Any additional request IDs for the window 09:00-09:45 PT would help.

We'll aim to come back with an initial root-cause hypothesis and a proposed credit calculation within the next 4 hours.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

Attachment: support_ticket_12345.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-04-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent partial degradation observed on /v1/generate - request for credit

Tessa / Marcus — preliminary correlation notes (internal):
- Our edge probes show increased 5xxs and elevated P95 latency during 09:06:00–09:38:40 PT, concentrated on egress toward AS43210 (EdgeCloud) peering.
- Redwood origin (in-region) CPU/memory/kv cache metrics show normal operating ranges; model hosts did not OOM or spike.
- We pulled the connection-level logs and saw intermittent TCP retransmits and ~1.2% packet loss on the peer path during the window.

Attachments: redwood_infra_synced_logs.zip (contains edge probe timeline + sampled request traces).

Initial hypothesis: partial degradation caused by upstream peering instability (EdgeCloud). Our telemetry suggests Redwood handled most requests, but the upstream packet loss led to increased client timeouts and retries that manifest as higher error rates for Helio. We should request EdgeCloud's peering logs for the same window and then apportion credit based on the duration and severity of the impact.

Suggested apportionment methodology (for discussion):
1) Count total affected seconds where client requests exceeded error/latency thresholds.
2) Compare our internal failure signatures vs. upstream loss signatures.
3) Split credit proportional to confirmed external loss time vs. internal service time.

Happy to draft the calculation once we have EdgeCloud's confirmation.

— Jonas
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@heliohealth.com>, ops@edgecloud.io
Cc: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-04-07T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Request to confirm peering event and propose preliminary credit calc

Hi Maria / EdgeCloud ops team —

Per our internal analysis (Jonas), telemetry points to a partial peering instability on the EdgeCloud path during ~09:06–09:38 PT that materially contributed to the elevated error rates Helio saw. To proceed to a mutual credit calculation we need EdgeCloud to confirm:
- Whether you observed packet loss/peering flap or maintenance in that time window;
- Your measured start/end times and severity; and
- Any internal/change events (config push, BGP updates) that might have caused the impact.

Proposed quick math (example):
- Window where Helio observed customer-visible errors: 09:05–09:40 (35 minutes)
- Confirmed upstream loss window (Redwood): 09:06–09:38 (32 minutes)
- Redwood service-level meters (internal): availability degraded ~18% for the 32-minute interval rather than full outage.

If EdgeCloud confirms a third-party partial outage for 32 minutes, our preliminary approach is to apportion uptime credit proportionally: attribute 60% of the visible degradation to upstream peering and 40% to residual internal impact (cache backoff and retries). That would convert to an agreed credit factor we can apply against the monthly uptime calculation.

Maria — does that approach look reasonable to you as an interim method? If so, we'll finalize once EdgeCloud provides their logs.

Thanks,
Tessa
From: EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.io>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com, maria.gonzalez@heliohealth.com
Date: 2028-04-07T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request to confirm peering event and propose preliminary credit calc

Hi Tessa / Maria —

We investigated and confirm there was a transient peering impairment on our metro exchange that affected a subset of prefixes (including the path to Redwood) between 09:05:50 and 09:38:22 PT. Root cause: a software bug in our route flap dampener that triggered an excessive withdraw affecting a small fanout. Severity: packet loss spikes up to ~1.6% on the affected paths, consistent with what Redwood observed.

We can share the peering report (attached: edgecloud_peering_report.txt) and are open to splitting responsibility. Our initial willingness is to accept 50% of the credit for the confirmed overlap window and work with Redwood on a joint customer-facing summary.

— EdgeCloud NOC
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@heliohealth.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, ops@edgecloud.io
Date: 2028-04-07T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-vector uptime credit for brief partial degradation on /v1/generate

Maria — thank you and thanks to EdgeCloud for the quick confirmation. Summary & next steps: 

1) Confirmed event window (mutual): 09:05:50–09:38:22 PT (32m32s).
2) EdgeCloud accepts 50% responsibility for the confirmed overlap window; Redwood accepts the remaining 50% based on residual internal service degradation signatures.
3) Proposed credit calculation: convert the 32m32s partial-degradation interval into an availability impact and apply a 50/50 split to the resulting credit. We will compute the credit amount against the April monthly invoice and issue a proportional service credit in the next billing cycle.
4) Redwood will provide the detailed calculation (line items and token counts) by EOD tomorrow and send a joint customer-ready incident summary once the numbers are finalized.

Please reply if any of the above is not agreeable. I'll follow up with the precise credit figure and the draft summary.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
